broken.title: Bare-flag re-apply in _applyRepairPaymentPool marks EVERY amount-matching row paid (no consume/once-tracking) → one owner paid-flag becomes TWO paid rows, inflating the eksoda dashboard paid total by a phantom 100%
broken.line: services/api/src/managers/buildingmanager.ts:3526-3535 (bare-flag loop) feeding the read at :4500 fromFlag = row.paid ? amount : 0 / :4501-4502 addPaid
broken.brokenShape: A split repair (chargeableTo 'split', tenantSharePercentage 50, actualCost 200) on a building with one vacant unit carrying the whole tenant side. First _distributeRepairCharge rebuilds TWO owner-side liability rows of the SAME amount: the owner-portion source:'repair' row (cost*(1-0.5) = 100) AND a source:'repair-vacant' row for the vacant unit (100). The landlord marks ONLY the owner-portion row paid via setOwnerExpensePaid (bare flag: row.paid=true, paidDate set, payments[] empty). Any innocuous repair edit (e.g. title change) re-runs _distributeRepairCharge. The snapshot loop (:3684-3686) captures bareFlagAmount = 100 (the one flagged row's amount). After strip+rebuild, _applyRepairPaymentPool's bare-flag loop (:3527-3535) iterates ALL liveRows and sets row.paid=true for EVERY row whose amount is within 0.005 of bareFlagAmount=100 — with NO once-tracking, NO consume(), and NO source/propertyId disambiguation. Both the rebuilt owner-portion 100 row AND the rebuilt repair-vacant 100 row match → BOTH marked paid. computeOwnerEksodaByMonth (:4500 fromFlag=row.paid?amount:0) then adds 100 paid for EACH of the two paid rows → paidByTerm = 200 against owed 200, reporting the repair fully settled when the owner only ever marked 100 as paid. Empirically reproduced: a standalone jest probe against the real module printed 'EKSODA owed=200 paid=200', 'PAID ROW COUNT: 2'. This is the same totalPaid/phantom-paid inflation class that the round-6 over-paid-row model was explicitly reverted to avoid (see the comment at :3556-3570), re-introduced through the round-4 bare-flag path (:3526) which lacks the cap/once-tracking the cash pool (:3543-3555) has. It misreports money the landlord has NOT paid as paid on the dashboard tile, hiding a 100 EUR outstanding liability. (Note: buildOwnerStatement at ownerstatement.ts:444-446 derives paid from payments[] not row.paid, so the legal statement is unaffected — but the in-app eksoda dashboard the landlord actually drives off is wrong.)
broken.trigger: 1) Split repair (or any repair) whose rebuild produces >=2 owner-side rows of equal amount. 2) Owner marks exactly ONE of them paid via the bare setOwnerExpensePaid flag (paid:true, empty payments). 3) Any subsequent _distributeRepairCharge run (innocuous edit / re-save). Result: both equal-amount rows get paid=true, eksoda paidByTerm double-counts the single flag.

verdict.reasoning: The skeptic's finding is REAL and I reproduced it end-to-end through the actual exported functions, not just by reasoning. Verified chain: (1) The bare-flag snapshot at :3684-3687 captures bareFlagAmount from ONLY the flagged row (one row => 100, not 200). (2) The re-apply loop at :3526-3535 is a pure predicate match over liveRows with NO consume/once-tracking and NO source/propertyId disambiguation — unlike the cash-pool fill at :3543-3554 which decrements `remaining` per row. So one owner paid-flag worth 100 lights up EVERY same-amount (100) liveRow. (3) In the symmetric split case (200 cost, 50% tenant share, one vacant unit carrying the whole tenant side), _distributeRepairCharge rebuilds two equal-amount owner rows: owner-portion 'repair' (100) and 'repair-vacant' (100). My E2E probe through the real _distributeRepairCharge confirmed BOTH get paid=true after an innocuous title re-edit (PAID ROW COUNT AFTER DISTRIBUTE: 2). (4) computeOwnerEksodaByMonth at :4500 reads fromFlag=row.paid?amount:0 and addPaid for each row, yielding owed=200 paid=200 — fully settled, outstanding 0 — when the owner only ever flagged 100 as paid. The 100 EUR repair-vacant liability is genuinely still owed but is hidden as paid on the in-app eksoda dashboard. This is exactly the totalPaid/phantom-paid inflation class the round-6 over-paid-row model was reverted to avoid, re-introduced through the round-4 bare-flag path which lacks the cap/consume the cash pool has. The leak is correctly scoped: the legal buildOwnerStatement (ownerstatement.ts:443-446) derives paid from payments[] and is unaffected; the damage is on computeOwnerEksodaByMonth, the surface the landlord drives in-app. Minimal precise leak: a single bare paid-flag on one repair row is duplicated onto every equal-amount sibling repair/repair-vacant row of the same repairId on the next distribute, double-counting paid on the eksoda dashboard and understating outstanding owner liability by the duplicated row amount. The fix would be to make the bare-flag re-apply consume bareFlagAmount per row (decrement, like the cash pool) and break once exhausted, rather than match unconditionally. Default verdict was HOLDS; it is overturned to BROKEN because I traced and empirically reproduced the exact wrong outcome.

broken.title: repair-vacant pool fill attributes a recorded καταβολή to the WRONG property/owner (multi-vacant-unit, array-order fill)
broken.line: buildingmanager.ts:3666-3690 (pool collapses per-property identity) + 3543-3555 (array-order capped fill) + ownermanager.ts:382-388,423 (per-property owner attribution)
broken.brokenShape: Building has two vacant units p1 (owner ΑΛΦΑ) and p2 (owner ΒΗΤΑ), both carrying a repair-vacant share of €25 for the same repair. The owner of p1 records a €25 καταβολή on p1's repair-vacant row; p2 is unpaid. The pre-strip pool sums ALL repair-vacant payments into ONE number (paidPool=25) and discards which propertyId paid it (3675-3683). On rebuild the two zero-payment repair-vacant rows are pushed in building.units order; _applyRepairPaymentPool fills them in array order capped per row (3543-3554), so the €25 lands on whichever row is FIRST in units[] — which can be p2's row. Total money is preserved, but the payment is now attributed to ΒΗΤΑ's unit, not ΑΛΦΑ's.
broken.trigger: Any repair add/edit (or any path calling _distributeRepairCharge) re-runs after a repair-vacant καταβολή was recorded, when ≥2 vacant units of DIFFERENT owners carry a share of the same repair and units[] order does not match which owner paid. On _aggregateOwners (ownermanager.ts:382-388) ΒΗΤΑ gets credited the €25 paid (totalPaid +25, outstanding 0) while ΑΛΦΑ keeps a €25 phantom outstanding — wrong owner ledger and wrong owner statement.

verdict.reasoning: The finding is REAL. I independently traced the exact path. Scenario: building.units = [p2(owner ΒΗΤΑ), p1(owner ΑΛΦΑ)] (insertion order, p2 first), a single split/tenant-charged repair where both units are vacant for the term so each carries a €25 repair-vacant share. ΑΛΦΑ records a €25 καταβολή — at record time payOwner lands it on p1's specific row resolved by ownerExpenseId (ownermanager.ts:756 `ownerMonthlyExpenses.id(a.ownerExpenseId)`), so attribution is initially CORRECT. Then ANY repair edit re-runs _distributeRepairCharge: (1) pre-strip pool sums €25 into paidPool with NO propertyId (3679/3690); (2) strip destroys p1's row _id (3709); (3) rebuild pushes two zero-payment repair-vacant rows in units order — p2's row FIRST, p1's second (3785 loop, 3844 push); (4) _applyRepairPaymentPool fills liveRows in array order capped per row (3543-3554), so the €25 lands on p2's row (first), capped at its €25 amount. The round-7 drop-surplus never fires because paidPool(25) < total liability(50) — no surplus. Read-side then attributes p2's row's paidAmount to ΒΗΤΑ (ownermanager.ts:382-383,423; ownerstatement.ts:433,442-445): ΒΗΤΑ gets totalPaid +25 / outstanding 0, while ΑΛΦΑ keeps a €25 phantom outstanding. Total money preserved (€25 still on a row, no negative outstanding, owed===amount per row, all clamps hold) — but the money is on the WRONG OWNER's ledger and statement/PDF. The asymmetry is deliberate and demonstrable: the C1 reattach path keys settlement by expenseId|propertyId|term (buildingmanager.ts:4011) and carries prior.propertyId (4062), so C1 cannot cross-attribute; the C2 repair-vacant pool drops propertyId, so it can. No test in ownerEksodaByMonth.test.js or repairCharges.test.js exercises two vacant units of DIFFERENT owners sharing one repair with a recorded payment, so the bug is uncovered. The trigger is purely units[] insertion-order-dependent (payer not first among vacant-sharing units) and fully reachable on any repair add/edit re-run. This is a genuine wrong-owner attribution leak, not money loss — but it ships wrong money to the wrong owner on the ledger, statement, and PDF.
verdict.correctedDetail: Minimal precise leak: in the multi-vacant-unit, different-owner case the unified repair-vacant pool re-attaches a recorded καταβολή to the FIRST repair-vacant row in building.units order rather than to the propertyId that actually paid, so the paid amount is credited to the wrong owner's ledger/statement (the paying owner keeps a phantom outstanding; the other owner shows a paid-off charge they never paid). Total euros preserved; attribution wrong. Minimal fix: make the repair-vacant portion of the pool propertyId-keyed (mirror C1's settleKey expenseId|propertyId|term at buildingmanager.ts:4011) — i.e., before the strip, capture a per-propertyId paid map for source==='repair-vacant' rows, and in _applyRepairPaymentPool fill each rebuilt repair-vacant row from its OWN propertyId's bucket (capped at amount) instead of the propertyId-blind scalar; keep the blind pool only for the building-wide source==='repair' owner-portion rows (which have propertyId null and one canonical owner, so order-fill is harmless there).

broken.title: bare manual paid-flag re-apply uses a SUMMED amount and can land on the WRONG row (or no row), un-paying flagged rows
broken.line: buildingmanager.ts:3684-3687 (bareFlagAmount += each flagged row's amount, SUMMED across repair + repair-vacant rows) + 3526-3535 (re-apply paid:true to a single row whose amount === the summed bareFlagAmount)
broken.brokenShape: Two repair-vacant rows for the same repair are each manually marked paid (setOwnerExpensePaid: paid:true, empty payments) — p1 €25, p2 €25. The pre-strip loop SUMS them into bareFlagAmount=50 (3685). On rebuild _applyRepairPaymentPool re-applies paid:true only to a row whose amount matches 50 (3529). Neither €25 row matches €50, so BOTH lose their paid flag (silently reverts two paid rows to outstanding). Worse: if the owner-portion 'repair' row happens to be €50, the flag lands on THAT (wrong) row while both €25 repair-vacant rows stay unpaid — wrong-row attribution.
broken.trigger: ≥2 owner-side rows of the same repair each bare-flagged paid (no payments[]) before any repair edit re-runs _distributeRepairCharge. The summed bareFlagAmount no longer matches any single rebuilt row, so the manual paid state is lost or misattributed — the exact B1/B2 regression the bare-flag carry was supposed to prevent, reintroduced for the multi-row case.

verdict.reasoning:
The finding is REAL. Independently traced the full path:

TRIGGER (achievable): A split/vacant repair distributes one repair-vacant row PER vacant unit (3843-3852), each with its own per-unit share amount. Example: two vacant units p1, p2 each €25. The breakdown panel exposes a per-row paid checkbox (2797). A landlord ticks BOTH via setOwnerExpensePaid (2919-2924), which sets paid:true with EMPTY payments[] on each row → two bare-flagged rows, paidPool=0.

CORRUPTION ON REBUILD: Any innocuous repair re-save re-runs _distributeRepairCharge. The pre-strip loop (3684-3687) SUMS the two flagged rows: bareFlagAmount = 25+25 = 50. After strip+rebuild there are again two fresh zero-payment €25 rows. The re-apply branch (3526-3535) requires a single row whose amount equals bareFlagAmount; |25 − 50| = 25 > 0.005 for BOTH rows → NEITHER is re-flagged. Both rebuilt rows end paid:false, payments:[].

MONEY/STATE OUTCOME: row.paid is the ONLY carrier of the bare-flag settlement state (payments[] is empty). It drives a real money number on the eksoda dashboard "owner-expenses paid" tile via fromFlag at 4500-4502 (€50 paid → €0), and the per-row paid checkbox on the breakdown panel via 2797 (both revert to unchecked). This is the exact B1/B2 "manually-checked-paid repair row reverted to outstanding on an innocuous repair edit" regression the bare-flag carry was built to prevent — reintroduced for the ≥2-same-repair-row case.

WRONG-ROW VARIANT also valid: if the owner-portion 'repair' row's amount happens to equal the SUM (€50), the flag lands on THAT untouched row while both €25 repair-vacant rows the landlord actually ticked stay unflagged — misattribution.

This is independent of the round-5/6/7 surplus-drop model: paidPool=0 in the no-payment case, so the pool/surplus logic is entirely bypassed; only the broken bare-flag branch runs. The single-row case (one flagged row whose amount equals bareFlagAmount) works, which is why the existing probe and B1/B2 single-row coverage pass and the multi-row sibling is an untested, genuinely broken path.

Minimal precise leak: bareFlagAmount must NOT be summed; it should be tracked PER bare-flagged row (e.g. a multiset/map of flagged amounts, or carry the flag per stripped row and re-match each rebuilt row to one consumed flag entry), so each rebuilt row of amount A re-derives paid from a flagged row of amount A — not from the sum of all flagged amounts. As written, any time ≥2 owner-side rows of one repair are bare-flagged and their amounts are unequal-or-don't-sum-to-a-single-row, the manual paid state is silently dropped or misattributed.

broken.title: Genuine owner OVERPAYMENT that a LATER recompute would re-owe is permanently dropped (surplus-drop is not reversible)
broken.line: buildingmanager.ts:3537-3554 (capped fill) + 3572-3579 (surplus dropped + logged, no remnant, no carry)
broken.brokenShape: Owner pays €200 toward a repair whose owner-portion is €200 (100% owners). Landlord later edits the repair to chargeableTo 'split' with 30% owner share for a brief moment (owner liability shrinks to €60), saves; pool fills the €60 row capped, drops €140 surplus (3572) and removes it from payments[] — it is NOT materialised anywhere. Landlord realizes the mistake and reverts the repair to 100% owners (€200 owed again). On this recompute the pool sums payments across rows = only the €60 that survived; the €140 is GONE from payments[] (it was never persisted — capped fill only attached €60, surplus was logged not stored). The repair now reads €200 owed / €60 paid / €140 outstanding — the owner's real €140 cash has been destroyed by a transient mis-edit.
broken.trigger: Any sequence that transiently shrinks the owner liability below the recorded payment (reclassify split↔owners, raise tenantSharePercentage, move-in) and then restores it. Because surplus is dropped from payments[] rather than parked, the NEXT recompute cannot recover it — paidPool only re-sums what was actually attached. The 'drop matches payOwner auto-mode' rationale holds for a one-shot overpay, but not for a reversible transition where the money was always legitimately the owner's.

verdict.reasoning: Independently traced and CONFIRMED. The surplus-drop at 3572-3579 is purely a logger.warn — the overpayment is NOT materialised in any payments[] array, not parked in a remnant row, not stored on the repair doc, nowhere. Because _distributeRepairCharge STRIPS all repair rows up front (3700-3710) and re-derives paidPool by summing only the surviving payments[] (3670-3690), the model is non-reversible w.r.t. recorded cash: any repair edit that transiently shrinks the owner-portion below recorded payments permanently truncates the payment to that smaller liability. Walking the skeptic's exact path: (1) €200 paid against a €200 100%-owner repair; (2) PATCH to split/30% owner → updateRepair(4947) runs _distributeRepairCharge, paidPool=200, rebuild a €60 row, capped fill writes payments=[€60], remaining=140 is logged-and-dropped (3572); the original €200 payment was already removed by the strip; (3) PATCH back to 100% owners → paidPool re-sums surviving payments[] = only €60, rebuild €200 row, fill €60. Read side (4495-4502) reports owed €200 / paid €60 / outstanding €140 — the owner is re-billed €140 of cash they actually paid, and nothing can recover it. recomputeOwnerExpensePaid (ownermanager 59-77) offers no recovery — it only re-derives paid from surviving payments. The fix's 'matches payOwner auto-mode surplus drop' rationale is sound for a GENUINE one-shot overpay (liability was always €60), but it is wrong for a REVERSIBLE liability transition where the €200 was correctly owed before and after — there the drop destroys legitimately-owed money. The trigger is two ordinary repair PATCHes (or a fat-finger-then-correct in one session), fully realistic. Notably the same fix's C1 path (4490-4493) made the OPPOSITE, safe choice (keep surplus in payments[], clamp only display); the repair path's destructive divergence is the leak. Default-BROKEN earned: exact wrong-money path traced to disk lines that match.
verdict.correctedDetail: Minimal precise leak: _applyRepairPaymentPool discards (logs-only, 3572-3579) any paidPool surplus beyond the current capped liability instead of persisting it. Because the next recompute rebuilds paidPool solely from surviving payments[] (3670-3690 after the strip at 3700-3710), the dropped euros can never be re-attached when a later edit re-enlarges the owner-portion. Fix options: (a) materialise the surplus into a settled-remnant 'repair' row (amount===remaining, payments=[remnant]) so it survives the next strip and re-pools — i.e. keep the round-1 remnant model for the reversible case; or (b) attach the surplus to the last-filled live row's payments[] as an over-paid row (the C1 policy at 4490-4493) so paidPool re-sums the full €200 next time, while every read surface already clamps paid=min(payments,amount) and outstanding=max(0,amount-paid). Either preserves the cash in payments[] and makes the transition reversible; the current code is the only model that physically deletes the money. The earlier r5/r6 reverts rejected the leaky read-side consequences of those models, but the correct lesson is to keep the cash in payments[] AND ensure ALL read surfaces clamp — not to delete the cash.

broken.title: Surplus-DROP on a TEMPORARY actualCost shrink permanently destroys a recorded owner καταβολή that a later recompute legitimately re-owes (NOT the same as the payOwner contract it claims to mirror)
broken.line: buildingmanager.ts:3572-3579 (_applyRepairPaymentPool surplus drop) — confirmed by empirical probe P5; read against ownermanager.ts:720-727 (payOwner auto-mode drop)
broken.brokenShape: An owner repair (chargeableTo:'owners', actualCost €200) is fully paid: a €200 καταβολή sits on the source:'repair' row. The landlord later edits actualCost DOWN to €50 (typo, or a partial-refund correction) and saves. _distributeRepairCharge pools paidPool=200, rebuilds a €50 liability row, fills it capped to €50, and the €150 surplus hits the logger.warn DROP at 3572 — the €150 is removed from payments[] entirely (no remnant row is written; the round-7 model deletes rather than parks it). The landlord then corrects actualCost back UP to €200. paidPool is now only €50, so paidByTerm reads €50 against owed €200. Probe P5 measured paid=50 (expected 200). The €150 the owner genuinely paid is gone from the document and unrecoverable.
broken.trigger: Repair fully paid (payment === current owner liability) → edit actualCost (or tenantSharePercentage) so the owner liability temporarily shrinks below the recorded payment → save → edit it back up → save. Each save runs _distributeRepairCharge; the first shrink-save destroys the surplus, the restore-save cannot recover it.

verdict.reasoning:
The skeptic's mechanical claim is REAL and I reproduced it empirically (afterShrink=50, afterRestore=50; the €150 is gone). The strip at buildingmanager.ts:3702-3710 physically removes the €200-bearing row and persists via b.save(); the surplus is dropped at :3572-3579 with only logger.warn (no remnant row in the round-7 model); and paidPool is re-captured only from persisted rows (:3670-3690), so a later restore-save cannot recover the destroyed €150.

The fix's defense — that this mirrors payOwner auto-mode's surplus drop — does NOT hold on read: (1) payOwner drops a transient TYPED input at payment-entry time and explicitly REPORTS the truncation to the user via allocatedTotal (ownermanager.ts:807-814), whereas the repair path silently destroys a previously-RECORDED καταβολή during an unrelated actualCost edit with zero UI feedback; (2) the read-side (ownermanager.ts:365-369) was deliberately built to display an over-paid row losslessly (outstanding floored at 0, paidAmount unclamped — "surplus stays visible as paidAmount"), so the reverted round-6 PARK model preserved the money AND was non-leaking on outstanding — the round-7 DROP discards money the read layer already tolerates; (3) the drop is destructive and irreversible against a liability the system cannot prove is permanent (the symmetric cost-up restore proves the €50 round-trips but the €150 does not). A single accidental low save permanently loses a recorded owner payment with no user-visible signal. That is precisely the silent money-loss class this review must catch, so the finding is confirmed and the fix is BROKEN for this shape. Minimal leak: on any actualCost/tenantSharePercentage edit that temporarily shrinks the owner liability below the recorded payment, the excess is deleted from payments[] permanently rather than parked on an over-paid live row (which the read side already renders correctly).

allVerdicts.evidence:

BUT the round-trip re-bill path defeats the "destroyed forever" claim:

- buildingmanager.ts:4171 vacant consume key `${expense._id}|${unit.propertyId}|${term}` and 4088 owner-fixed consume key `${expense._id}||${term}` — BOTH byte-equal the remnant's settleKey (for owner-fixed, propertyId null → String(null||'')='' → key 'e||T' matches '${id}||${term}').
- buildingmanager.ts:4177 amount: Math.round(share*100)/100 (vacant) / 4094 amount: ownerAmount (owner-fixed) — the rebuilt row's amount is re-derived from the LIVE expense, NOT from the remnant.

allVerdicts.leak: Minimal precise leak: _applyRepairPaymentPool discards (logs-only, 3572-3579) any paidPool surplus beyond the current capped liability instead of persisting it. Because the next recompute rebuilds paidPool solely from surviving payments[] (3670-3690 after the strip at 3700-3710), the dropped euros can never be re-attached when a later edit re-enlarges the owner-portion. Fix options: (a) materialise the surplus into a settled-remnant 'repair' row (amount===remaining, payments=[remnant]) so it survives the next strip and re-pools — i.e. keep the round-1 remnant model for the reversible case; or (b) attach the surplus to the last-filled live row's payments[] as an over-paid row (the C1 policy at 4490-4493) so paidPool re-sums the full €200 next time, while every read surface already clamps paid=min(payments,amount) and outstanding=max(0,amount-paid). Either preserves the cash in payments[] and makes the transition reversible; the current code is the only model that physically deletes the money. The earlier r5/r6 reverts rejected the leaky read-side consequences of those models, but the correct lesson is to keep the cash in payments[] AND ensure ALL read surfaces clamp — not to delete the cash.

allVerdicts.title: The surplus-DROP design is justified by 'matches payOwner auto-mode', but payOwner never DELETES an already-recorded payment — it only declines to record an unallocatable one; the pool destroys persisted, previously-reconciled money
allVerdicts.line: buildingmanager.ts:3556-3570 (justification comment) vs ownermanager.ts:713-728 (actual payOwner surplus path)
allVerdicts.leak: The skeptic's title is half-right and should be narrowed: the drop DOES destroy persisted money (unlike payOwner), so the comment's analogy is imperfect. But the destroyed euro is, at drop time, a genuine OVERPAYMENT beyond the correctly-computed current liability (buildingmanager.ts:3543-3554 fill every live row to its own amount first; remaining>0 means paidPool exceeded Σ current liability). It is never money currently owed. totalPaid (ownermanager.ts:423, unclamped) reads CORRECTLY low because the surplus is not in payments[] — this is the intended leak-freedom, not an under-report bug, since outstanding is also 0 (owed===paid). The single genuine loss is an owner cash overpayment against a permanently-shrunk liability with no refund record — the documented no-owner-carry-forward limitation that payOwner shares (logger.info-only drop, ownermanager.ts:723-726), not a money-correctness defect this fix introduces. No surface double-counts, inflates, or goes negative; the realistic payment≤liability C2 bug is fully preserved.
